 Harry Brook keen to add to happy MCG memories when T20 series starts
 England have landed the first blow in their white-ball tour, coming fro.m behind to take the ODI series 2-1

 Harry Brook is hoping to make more good memories at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, with England kicking off their T20 series against Australia at the same venue they became world champions four years ago.
 The fabled MCG has not always been a happy hunting ground for touring England sides but Brook’s last two visits have been triumphant.
 A two-day win at the 90,000 venue in last year’s Boxing Day Test was not only the high point of a traumatic Ashes campaign, it was their first red-ball victory on Australian soil since 2011.
 open image in gallery England won the T20 World Cup at the MCG in 2022 (PA Archive/PA) ( PA Archive ) And it also played host to England’s T20 World Cup win 2022, where Brook was part of the side that defeated Pakistan to lift the trophy behind enemy lines.
 Brook is one of four survivors from that day, joined by Adil Rashid , Phil Salt and Sam Curran – who capped a fine tournament by being named player of the match in the final.
 “We walked in earlier and a few of us said ‘there’s some good memories here’. It’s good to be back,” he said.
 “Sam’s excited, he was the one that actually mentioned it when we went in the changing room. We’re all really looking forward to it. Obviously that Ashes win was a very good one too and to be able to win a Test at the MCG was an incredible achievement from us.”
 England have landed the first blow in their white-ball tour, coming from behind to take the ODI series 2-1, but both sides have a distinctly unfamiliar look heading into the five-match T20 leg.
 open image in gallery Thomas Rew, 18, is a new arrival in the England squad (Robbie Stephenson/PA) ( PA Archive ) Joe Root, Ben Duckett, Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker have all departed ahead of next month’s Test series in South Africa, leaving room for fresh faces to press their claims.
 James Coles, Eddie Jack, Henry Crocombe and 18-year-old Thomas Rew all await potential debuts in the next two weeks, while Aneurin Donald deputises for the injured Jos Buttler at opener.
 England, though, will not be blooding them for the sake of it as they look to keep their momentum – and the world number one status that they have been passing back and forward with India for the past year.
 “It’s awesome, they’re all really excited and it’s exciting to have them here as well, to be able to get those lads in and have the opportunity to be in and around an England squad,” Brook added.
 “In this series we still want to be world number one again. We’re on a really good run, we’re playing really good cricket and we’ve come out here to try and win this series. There’ll be some opportunities for guys that haven’t played before but we’re trying to pick the best XI.”
 Brook and Jordan Cox will be joining the list of departures before the fifth and final match of the series, leaving Will Jacks to captain in his absence, and Brook is hopeful of getting on the plane with another success under his belt.
 “It would be nice to win 4-0 before I leave, obviously, but we’ll just stay in the moment, play what’s in front of us and hopefully the games go our way.”
